title: Quantization Profile Library (MVP) — Applied ML working notes
body:
Doc purpose
- Working notes for MVP quantization profile library (Redwood-published profiles only).
- Capture candidate profiles, calibration/eval TODOs, open questions, and early benchmark pointers.
- Not a spec. Expect churn.

Owners / who to bug
- Profiles / methodology: Arjun D.
- Pipeline / artifacts: Priyanka B.
- Evals + gates: Jonas W. (+ Selene H. for guardrails)
- Harness integration: Olivia G.
- Perf methodology: Claire D.
- Runtime compat: Mateo A. / Hiro T.

Current MVP framing (rough)
- Target: ship 1–2 model families w/ 2 quant variants each (int8 and “safe int4” only where we have strong gating).
- Opt-in, route-scoped enablement only.
- Must have conservative defaults, rollback-ready, and clear scoping by GPU arch + kernel constraints.

Candidate model list (proposed for MVP)
Notes:
- We need to align with runtime support + perf suite coverage (A100 + H100 first; L4 maybe if stable).
- Prefer models already heavily used in Hosted and in benchmark lab.

Table (draft)
Model family | Baseline | Quant variants to publish | Notes / risk
1) Llama 3.1 8B Instruct | bf16 | int8 (W8A8) + int4 (weight-only) | int4 likely route-limited (summarization, non-tool-calling) pending JSON/tool gating
2) Llama 3.1 70B Instruct | bf16 | int8 (W8A8) | int4 probably too risky for MVP; keep as stretch
3) Qwen2.5 7B Instruct | bf16 | int8 | good candidate for “fast cheap” routes, but promptset coverage is thinner vs Llama
4) Mistral Large (open) | fp16/bf16 | int8 | TBD; kernel path risk + context length perf variance

Decision needed (PM + runtime): MVP should be “Llama-only” vs “Llama + 1 smaller alt model”.
- My bias: Llama 3.1 8B + 70B only, to reduce matrix explosion.

Hardware scoping assumptions (for artifact manifests)
- GPU targets: A100 (sm80), H100 (sm90) for MVP. Add L4 (sm89) only if we can validate kernels and avoid surprise p95 regressions.
- Kernel families in play (runtime):
  - int8: fp8-style kernels are out of scope; stick to known stable W8A8 path.
  - int4: weight-only path w/ limited activation quant; must clearly specify supported sequence length bins.
- Manifest needs explicit compatibility: (gpu_arch, driver range?, cuda major, kernel_id, max_context_tokens tested).

Calibration notes (draft)
We need consistent calibration rules so profiles are comparable + repeatable.

Calibration dataset candidates
- “Redwood-calib-v1”: mixture of summarization + Q/A + instruction following + structured output attempts.
- Must include:
  - long context (8k–32k) tokens: retrieval-ish prompts + summarization over long inputs
  - JSON mode/tool calling style: at least 15–20% of calibration and eval prompts, even if int4 not targeted for those routes

Open question: do we calibrate per-context-bin?
- Option A: one calibration set for all lengths (simpler)
- Option B: separate calibration for long-context (more work but may avoid long-context drift)
Action: Jonas + Priyanka to test A vs B on 8B int4.

Quant methods under consideration (what we mean in profile docs)
- int8 (W8A8): target “general safe default”; should be eligible for interactive chat routes if quality gates pass.
- int4 (weight-only): target “batch / cost-sensitive”; likely disable by default for JSON/tool routes.
- For each published profile we must include:
  - calibration version id
  - eval harness run ids
  - perf suite run ids
  - known-bad features (structured output strictness, tool-calling reliability, long context)

Early results (VERY preliminary, do not cite externally)
These are notes from benchmark lab runs + ad-hoc harness tests. Values are directional.

Llama 3.1 8B
- int8:
  - p50 latency: ~10–20% better on A100 for typical 1–2k prompts; p95 variance depends on batching.
  - tokens/$: improved; biggest wins in high QPS w/ continuous batching.
  - quality: small deltas; JSON-mode strictness sometimes worse (missing quotes/trailing commas) under certain prompt patterns.
- int4 weight-only:
  - perf win: significant for batch summarization loads, but long-context shows mixed results (memory bandwidth bound vs compute).
  - quality: noticeable drift on tool calling + structured outputs; plain summarization looks okay.

Llama 3.1 70B
- int8:
  - perf: meaningful cost reduction; but kernel selection sensitive to seq length. Need explicit seq bins in profile.
  - quality: early indication OK on “general assistant” prompts; still need targeted safety + JSON.

Pointers to early perf runs
- benchmark-lab report ids (internal):
  - blab://quant/2024-11-18/llama31-8b-int8-a100-sm80-run07
  - blab://quant/2024-11-22/llama31-8b-int4-a100-sm80-run03
  - blab://quant/2024-12-05/llama31-70b-int8-h100-sm90-run02

Pointers to early eval runs
- eval-harness comparison job ids (internal):
  - eh://compare/2024-11-20/llama31-8b/baseline-bf16-vs-int8-profileA
  - eh://compare/2024-11-27/llama31-8b/baseline-bf16-vs-int4-profileW
  - eh://compare/2024-12-10/llama31-70b/baseline-bf16-vs-int8-profileB

Quality gates / TODOs (Applied ML + Evals)
High priority (must do before publishing any profile)
- Define pass/fail thresholds per route category (interactive chat vs background/batch vs JSON/tooling).
- Expand prompt set coverage for:
  - tool calling (function selection accuracy + argument JSON validity)
  - strict JSON mode (valid JSON parse rate)
  - long context (>=16k) factuality + “don’t drop details” tests
  - refusal/safety checks (ensure quant doesn’t increase policy violations)
- Add “format regression” checks: regex/parseable outputs, schema adherence.
- Add statistical test policy for borderline deltas (Jonas to confirm: bootstrap CI? paired t-test?).

Medium priority
- Add targeted multilingual prompts (at least top 5 langs by traffic).
- Add code generation subset (light) to detect obvious degradation.

Known failure modes we’ve observed (keep in mind when building gates)
- JSON-mode: extra prose outside JSON, trailing commas, unescaped characters.
- Tool calling: correct tool but wrong args keys; or tool name drift.
- Long context summarization: higher omission rate, especially with enumerated lists.

Perf validation / TODOs (Perf suite)
- Ensure perf suite covers:
  - sequence length bins: 256, 1k, 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k (if supported)
  - concurrency shapes: low QPS interactive; high QPS batch
  - streaming vs non-streaming (runtime path differences)
- Ensure we capture:
  - time-to-first-token (TTFT)
  - tokens/sec steady-state
  - p95/p99 tail under load
  - GPU memory usage and KV cache interactions

Runtime + profile artifact TODOs (for Priyanka / Quentin / Mateo)
- Decide naming conventions:
  - profile_id: model + quant method + calibration version + kernel family + gpu arch
  - profile_version: semver; bump minor on metadata-only changes? (likely patch)
- Ensure manifest includes:
  - “tested_on”: gpu_arch + driver/cuda + runtime version
  - “constraints”: max_context, supported dtype, known_issues
  - “fallback”: baseline ref + conditions
- Artifact signing process: confirm keys + verification in runtime (security thread w/ Marcus L.).

Open questions (need answers to avoid churn)
1) Route categories: who owns canonical taxonomy?
   - We keep saying “interactive chat”, “batch summarization”, “JSON/tool routes”. Is there a route label system we can reliably use in policy evaluation?
   - Action: sync with Mina H. / Ravi M. on what routing policy can read.

2) What is acceptable regression in structured outputs?
   - Is it a hard requirement that JSON parseable rate stays within X%? Or do we allow small dips if customer opts in?
   - My suggestion: for JSON/tool routes we require near-parity; if not, we block enabling quant on those routes.

3) Profile selection by sequence length
   - Do we publish one profile that includes per-length kernel params, or multiple profiles per length regime?
   - Risk: too many artifacts; but single artifact may hide perf cliffs.

4) How do we handle customers pinning profile versions?
   - Requirement: route-level pin should survive profile updates (unless forced rollback).
   - Need policy for “security hotfix” profile revocations.

5) int4 scope
   - Do we allow int4 only for specific “safe” models and only for non-JSON routes in MVP?
   - If yes, we should hardcode guardrail recommendations in docs/console warnings.

6) Calibration privacy / dataset storage
   - Where does calibration data live? Who can access? (we should avoid accidental inclusion of customer data).

7) Mixed-precision / hybrid approaches
   - Out of scope for MVP, but we should decide if profiles can specify layer-wise exceptions (keep embeddings/final layers bf16).

Next steps (next 2 weeks)
- Arjun + Priyanka: finalize candidate models + profile shortlist for MVP (by 2024-12-23).
- Jonas + Selene: propose concrete quality gates per route category + draft exception process.
- Olivia: confirm eval harness can output a single “publish gate” boolean + attach artifacts to profile publish workflow.
- Claire: lock perf suite matrix (GPU + seq bins) and confirm runtime version pinned for comparisons.
- Mateo + Hiro: confirm kernel availability/stability for int4 on A100; document incompatibilities.

Meeting notes snippets (raw)
2024-11-14 (Applied ML standup)
- Arjun: “int8 is straightforward, int4 is where we get weirdness on JSON.”
- Jonas: “we need prompt set coverage before we even argue thresholds.”
- Priyanka: “artifact schema must force hardware scoping or we will repeat the mis-scoped incident.”

2024-12-03 (Evals sync)
- Selene: “route-level allowlist for int4 might be the safest default: only summarization routes initially.”
- Olivia: eval harness can run baseline vs quant with paired prompts; need a stable prompt id system.

Loose ends / notes to self
- Make sure we tag eval failures by failure type (format vs content) so we don’t overreact to benign drift.
- Console UX warnings should be backed by actual data: link to dashboard view filtered by route+profile.
- Ask SRE what auto-disable signal they want (5xx? parse errors? user feedback? internal eval drift?)
